checks: Both sign sums have bounded positive densities on their own open half-lines, so the reflected convolution is continuous and positive everywhere. The actual linear-section coarea denominator and coordinate first moments are finite and positive by eliminating a nonzero coordinate and retaining exponential domination. Zero-coefficient coordinates remain independent.

The exact tilt changes the independent rates to beta_i(t) on I, and the coordinate dilation preserves the scalar value V. On the zero section the tilt is constant and the linear Jacobian cancels upon conditional normalization, giving the actual section means and density, not only almost-everywhere disintegration data.

The two half-transforms sum to the moment generating function 1/Z(t). Multiplication of rates yields both quotient formulas. As an independent two-phase check, for coefficients (2,-3) and t=1/4, the old means are (3/5,2/5), the new means (3/10,7/10), and the new nonnegative-side probability is 7/10, matching the formulas exactly.

Prékopa convolution and multiplication by the exponential tilt give positive log-concave half-densities with finite moments. The cited second-moment inequality gives (1/A)''≥0 and (1/B)''≥0. For H/(1-pt), the sign of its derivative is the sign of N, with N'=(1-pt)H''≥0. Taking the reciprocal reverses the monotonicity, including flat portions and monotone whole-interval cases.
